content: This file only contains a single declaration, which is an instance whose proof is inferInstance, and a lot of mathematical description. The only reason I can think of for this file to exist is that this instance somehow speeds up typeclass search. If that is true, then that should be documented, and much of the mathematical "documentation" removed as it is confusing.
This file used to have proofs, as you can check the history of it. The proof is removed after a refactor, as it is described in the mathematical "documentation".
I guess I'm asking - should the file be removed?
That's subtle; I cannot give a definite answer.
Or, maybe in order to use inferInstance you need to import several files to get all the necessary instances. So it's convenient to have a single file for that instance.
Is this a common pattern? Normally we just.. import both files downstream.

Artie Khovanov said:

Is this a common pattern?

I don't think so. I think it is just a historical reason.
When I proved this orzechProperty was not even a thing, so feel free to remove the file and see what happens.

If there are performance reasons to keep the shortcut instance, its priority should be bumped above the longer instance derivation (currently both are at priority 100), and the documentation should be updated to make it clear there's no new content there.

+0.03% overall instructions generally is significant (although the precise number has noise in the order of 10^10 instructions or so). Looks like the relevant PR #12076 did not say why the instance was kept. I think the right way to go here is indeed to keep the shortcut instance, with appropriate documentation, at a priority of 200 perhaps.
Note that instance synthesis goes fastest when the hierarchy is wide, not deep. So it makes sense that this kind of shortcut (which skips over one level) will cause speedup.

No we didn't benchmark it.
